Theme

Latin word

quī

quī, qua (quae), quod

adjective (the indefinite quī) · Wiktionary

any (after sī, nisi, num, nē); how? how ever?; what … ? (with a noun); which? what? (with a noun); who, which, that

In this lexicon

  • any

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.7: num quod officium aliud aliō majus sit (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.48: sī quī graviōre vulnere acceptō equō dēciderat (Lewis & Short)

  • how

    also used · classical · Ter. And. 302: Quī scīs?; Phaedr. 1.1.7: quī possum, quaesō, facere quod quereris, lupe?

  • what

    also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.7.5: quō cibō

  • which

    the recommended word · classical · Phaedr. 3.7.5: aut quō cibō fēcistī tantum corporis?

  • which

    the recommended word · classical · Catull. 3.5: quem plūs illa oculīs suīs amābat; Phaedr. 1 prol. 1: Aesōpus auctor quam māteriam repperit

  • Is est amīcus quī in rē dubiā rē juvat.: a friend in need is a friend indeed

    classical

  • sunt quī (+ subjunctive): certain

    classical

  • quī rērum potiuntur: government

    classical

  • Sōlus omnīnō est quī sine amīcō est.: he is utterly alone who has no friend

    medieval

  • quī audiunt: listener

    classical

  • is quī interest: participant

    classical

  • quī reī pūblicae praeest: president

    classical

  • is quī loquitur (dīcit): speaker

    classical

  • quī linguam mordet: spicy

    modern

  • carrus quī trahitur: trailer

    * our formation

  • Ille dolet vērē quī sine teste dolet.: true grief is a private matter

    classical

  • is quī injūriam accēpit: victim

    classical

  • Frūstrā labōrat quī omnibus placēre studet.: you can’t please everybody

    modern
